title: GPTQ: Accurate Post-Training Quantization for Generative Pre-trained Transformers
layout_note: Two matrix panels side by side (the inverse Hessian in Cholesky form on the left, the weight matrix on the right) joined by a double-headed arrow, with a two-entry legend box spanning the bottom.
grouping: Each panel has a bold sans-serif title above and a plain one- or two-line caption below; no frames around the panels. Colour families carry state: peach/orange = quantized weights, blue/light blue = not yet quantized weights that get updated, with the darker shade marking the current block.
shapes_depth: Flat, square corners, black outlines. The Hessian is a square whose lower-left triangle is grey with a staircase edge (the Cholesky factor) and whose upper part is pale blue; the weight matrix is a tall rectangle cut into vertical colour stripes. A thick black outline frames the current block in both matrices, and one white row/column marks the column being processed.
proposed_highlight: The current block is outlined with a heavy black rectangle in both matrices and filled in the saturated shades (orange, deep blue), while finished and pending parts stay pale.
lesson: Show a column-by-column algorithm on a matrix by colouring stripes by state (done, current, pending) and outlining the current block with the same heavy frame in every matrix it touches.
notes: elements 'other' = the heavy black outline around the current block. Venue from the first page ('Published as a conference paper at ICLR 2023'); arXiv id is 2022. Method builds on Optimal Brain Quantization (OBQ); GPTQ is treated as its own paradigm here.

arrangement.units: two unframed matrix panels side by side, each with a bold title above and a short plain caption below
arrangement.inputs_as: no separate inputs; the two matrices themselves are the objects
arrangement.shared: the current block is marked in both matrices with the same heavy outline, and a double-headed arrow links the two

taxonomy.note: architecture 'other' = a layer-wise quantization procedure on one weight matrix; no network is drawn

core.what: The algorithm drawn on the two matrices it uses: the inverse Hessian's Cholesky factor (grey staircase triangle) on the left and the weight matrix as column stripes on the right, the current block framed heavily in both and joined by a double-headed arrow.

relations.form: two equal-sized matrices side by side as rectangles; the Hessian's lower part a grey staircase, the weights vertical stripes whose shade says quantized (orange) or still to be updated (blue)
a heavy black frame around block i in the weight matrix and around the matching rows of the Hessian, with a double-headed arrow between the two frames
column order left to right in the weight matrix: pale orange finished, saturated orange current-quantized, a white column being quantized, saturated blue current-pending, pale blue later columns

channels.colour: weight status, keyed in the bottom legend: orange = quantized, blue = unquantized and being updated; saturation adds a second meaning, in or out of the current block; the Hessian's blue shades reuse the weight blues without a key for what they mean there
channels.shape: rectangle = matrix, staircase = triangular Cholesky factor
channels.line: heavy black frame = current block (one meaning, used in both matrices); double-headed arrow = the two are used together
channels.frame: heavy black rectangle = the active block

quality.strengths: The method's lazy block update is drawn as geometry on the matrices themselves: one heavy frame marks the same block in both, and column colour shows the quantized / pending boundary moving left to right; the legend is one strip.
quality.weaknesses: Saturation carries a second meaning (inside the current block) that is not keyed; the Hessian's blue shading has no stated meaning; the white column under quantization is unlabeled; the double-headed arrow says only 'related', not which direction information flows.

insights.structure: Two matrices sit side by side as equals, the inverse Hessian on the left and the weight block on the right, joined by a double-headed arrow and keyed by one bottom legend.
insights.data: Matrices are drawn as plain rectangles: the Hessian's Cholesky factor is a grey staircase triangle and the weight matrix is vertical colour stripes whose hue says quantized or pending.
insights.emphasis: A heavy black frame around the current block, repeated on the matching rows of the Hessian, plus saturated orange/blue shades set the active block apart from pale finished and pending parts.
insights.flow: Read the two bold titles left to right, then the captions below each; the only connector is a horizontal double-headed arrow with no label.
insights.avoid: The double-headed arrow carries no label, so what passes between the Hessian and the weights is left to the caption.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
